goal.what: Whoever builds or changes Lane, a person or an AI, makes it give the developer AI what it comes for: subagents that keep the rules of their steps, and an orchestrator that starts them in the order set, on every run, with no check code or script of its own.
grounds: plugins/turn/best-practices/ux.json, standard.goal: "Whoever builds or changes the product, a person or an AI, makes it give its users what they come for."

plugins/lane/README.md:6-9: "With Lane, your subagents keep the rules of their steps on every run, and your orchestrator, the subagent that starts the others, starts them in your order, which you write as a flow. You write no code for the checks and no script for the order."

decisions.decided: The developer AI: an AI that builds a Claude Code plugin whose subagents work in numbered steps. The one who later runs that plugin comes to the plugin, not to Lane, and is no user of Lane's.
grounds: plugins/lane/README.md:6: "Lane is for you, an AI that builds a Claude Code plugin whose subagents work in numbered steps."
dev/lane/architecture.md:67: "Whoever runs the plugin did not choose Lane"

decisions.what: Where does the reader learn the words of Lane's that they have not used: developer AI, rule, orchestrator, flow and move?
decisions.decided: In one paragraph under the title, before the OKRs, so that each objective stays one short sentence. A rule is a sentence in a step that the subagent must keep; the orchestrator is the subagent that starts the others; the flow is the order it starts them in, with the answers that send the work back, which the developer AI sets; a move is one start of a subagent the flow names.
grounds: plugins/turn/best-practices/refactor-doc.json Q6 steps: "For a word the document must keep, give its meaning in a few everyday words, in the sentence where the reader first meets it."
plugins/turn/best-practices/ux.json, format objective: "one short sentence of what a user gets from the product, with the user as its subject."
plugins/lane/README.md:11: "A rule is a sentence in a step, such as ``Do not run `git commit` or `git push`.``, with a check of it."
plugins/lane/docs/flow.md:7: "A flow is the order in which one subagent of your plugin, the orchestrator, starts the others"

decisions.what: How many objectives, and cut by what?
decisions.decided: Two: the rules of each step kept (O1), and the subagents started in the order set (O2). A plugin can have rules with no flow, or a flow with no rules, so each piece of work on Lane brings one of them closer.
grounds: plugins/lane/README.md:3-4: "so that they keep the rules of their steps and start one another in the order that you set."
plugins/lane/docs/lanes.md:112-113: "A proposal may hold a flow alone, with no `subagents`."

decisions.decided: O1: The developer AI has its subagents keep the rules of their steps on every run, with no check code of its own.
grounds: plugins/turn/best-practices/ux.json Q1 steps: "Write it as one sentence: that user as its subject, then a verb, its object and the context it is done in, with no feature or mechanism of the product."
plugins/lane/README.md:8-9: "You write no code for the checks"

decisions.decided: O2: The developer AI has its orchestrator start the other subagents in the order of its flow on every run, with no script of its own for the order.
grounds: as D4
plugins/lane/README.md:9: "and no script for the order."

decisions.what: What does each key result count?
decisions.decided: What the developer AI's subagents do on runs, as a share out of a named whole, or what the developer AI spends, in lines of code or in time; never a count of Lane's output, such as rules laid. Each says which direction is better, and none has a target value.
grounds: plugins/turn/best-practices/ux.json Q3 steps: "Turn each sign kept into one measure, a share, an average per user, a count or a time, and name what it is counted out of."
plugins/turn/best-practices/ux.json Q3 steps: "drop counts of output, such as features shipped or tasks done."

decisions.decided: KR1.1: of the tool calls and ends of work that break a rule, the share that goes through. KR1.2: of those the rules allow, the share that is stopped. KR1.3: of the breaks stopped, the share after which the subagent still does not keep the rule, such as by trying another way. KR1.4: the lines of code the developer AI writes by hand for a plugin so that its subagents keep the rules. KR1.5: the time from the developer AI's first rule for a plugin to the first run in which its subagents keep the rules. Lower, fewer and shorter are better.
grounds: KR1.1 alone gets better by stopping everything; KR1.2 holds it to the user's gain (ux.json Q3 steps: "Ask whether all the objective's key results could get better while the user still does not get what the objective says").
plugins/lane/README.md:13-14: "A hook that only refuses a call leaves the subagent to look for another way", the failure KR1.3 counts.
D4's "with no check code of its own" is counted by KR1.4; the time to the first run that keeps the rules is what laying them costs.

decisions.decided: KR2.1: of the runs, the share in which the subagents are not started in the order of the flow. KR2.2: of the orchestrator's tool calls and ends of work that the flow allows, the share that is stopped. KR2.3: the lines of code the developer AI writes by hand for a plugin so that the subagents start in the order of the flow. KR2.4: the time from the developer AI's first flow for a plugin to the first run that keeps it. Lower, fewer and shorter are better.
grounds: A run that starts one subagent out of order fails O2, so KR2.1 counts runs; it counts what the developer AI sees, the order the subagents start in, whether the orchestrator strays or Lane reads an answer wrong.
KR2.2 holds KR2.1 as KR1.2 holds KR1.1; KR2.3 and KR2.4 count what O2 spares, as KR1.4 and KR1.5 do.

decisions.what: Which comes first, a break let through or an allowed call stopped (KR1.1 and KR1.2, KR2.1 and KR2.2)?
decisions.decided: The break let through, or the run out of order, comes first: KR1.1 before KR1.2, and KR2.1 before KR2.2. A break that goes through is what the rule is there to stop, while a subagent stopped on an allowed call is told why and tries again.
grounds: dev/lane/architecture.md:47: "When the check script cannot check a call or an end, it stops it."
dev/lane/architecture.md:52: "A call let through unchecked could be the break the rule is there to stop"
plugins/lane/docs/flow.md:116-118: "While a move is due, the orchestrator is told the sentence and the move on the next line: at PreToolUse, on a call that is not the move, which is stopped"

decisions.what: Which comes first, what the runs meet or what the developer AI spends (KR1.1 and KR1.2 against KR1.4 and KR1.5, KR2.1 and KR2.2 against KR2.3 and KR2.4)?
decisions.decided: What the runs meet comes first: KR1.1 and KR1.2 each come before KR1.4 and KR1.5, and KR2.1 and KR2.2 each before KR2.3 and KR2.4. A wrong check acts on every run, while the developer AI spends the lines and the time once for each plugin. A change that moves them apart is one such as reading another text format without the code that describes it, or checking a proposal less to lay it faster.
grounds: D4 and D5: "on every run" is the objective; the code and the time are what it spares.

plugins/lane/README.md:28-29: "Lane reads the texts your plugin writes, such as a list of items to answer, in one format only. For another format, you write an adapter": Lane already spends the developer AI's lines to keep its checks right.
plugins/turn/best-practices/ux.json Q7 thinking: "the one whose loss keeps the user further from the objective comes first."

decisions.what: Which plugin do the scenarios run on?
decisions.decided: The example plugin changelog, which writes a project's CHANGELOG.md, as the README's walkthrough runs it; its subagents lead, the orchestrator, writer, which writes the new entries, and reviewer, which compares the entries with the commits.
grounds: .claude/rules/dev.md step 1: "the README takes two things from the UX: what the user gains, and the scenario that its walkthrough runs."
plugins/lane/README.md:62-63: "The plugin `changelog` writes a project's `CHANGELOG.md`"

decisions.what: Who takes part, and of what kind?
decisions.decided: The developer AI (an AI), which also runs changelog to try it; lay.py, Lane's script it runs (a script); the check script that lay.py puts into changelog (a script); lead, writer and reviewer (AIs). No step on the main paths waits for a person.
grounds: plugins/lane/README.md:104: "When you ask `changelog` for an entry and a commit, it runs `writer`."
plugins/lane/README.md:116: "Lane puts its checks into your plugin as one script, the check script"

decisions.what: What does the document show of Lane, and what does it leave to the architecture?
decisions.decided: Only what the developer AI runs, sees and receives, and what its subagents are told: lay.py's commands and what they show, and the check script as one participant that lets calls through, stops them and tells moves. No hook event, file inside Lane or Claude Code mechanism by which a line reaches a subagent.
grounds: plugins/turn/best-practices/ux.json Q6 steps: "Treat the product as one box, and flag each participant named for a piece of it that the user does not run, see or receive."
dev/lane/architecture.md:150-218 draws the hooks and modules behind the same paths.

decisions.what: How is a line that a subagent is told, or that lay.py shows, given?
decisions.decided: As its exact text, a line told headed by the plugin's name, so that a builder reads what the developer AI and its subagents read, and a change to the text shows as a change to the UX.
grounds: plugins/lane/hooks/lane/hook.py:163 heads each line a check tells with the plugin's name, as `{plugin}: {s.text}`.
What a subagent reads is what the developer AI's run meets; a paraphrase cannot be checked against the code.
plugins/lane/README.md:88 gives step 3 as lay.py print shows it: "Write only `CHANGELOG.md`. Do not run `git commit` or `git push`."

decisions.decided: With the objective's ID and a short phrase, the developer AI its subject and its verb active: "O1: The developer AI holds writer to two rules of its step" and "O2: The developer AI has lead start writer and reviewer in its flow's order".
grounds: plugins/turn/best-practices/ux.json Q5 steps: "write a heading with its ID and a short phrase, the user its subject and its verb active, saying how they reach it."

decisions.decided: The developer AI asks lay.py print for two rules on step 3 of writer, write only CHANGELOG.md and do not run git commit or git push, and sees step 3 as it will be; once it approves, lay.py write writes step 3 and puts the check script into changelog. It asks changelog for an entry and a commit; writer writes CHANGELOG.md, the check script lets it through, and writer ends with CHANGELOG.md written and no commit, as step 3 now says. No stop is drawn: the main path leaves stops off, and the README has writer keep the rule by reading the step.
grounds: plugins/lane/README.md:104-106: "`writer` writes `CHANGELOG.md`, and the check lets it through. `writer` reads the new sentences in step 3, and ends without a commit. If `writer` runs `git commit`, the check stops the call"
plugins/turn/best-practices/ux.json Q5 steps: "Choose the main path from that request to that end, the one most users take, and leave failures and stops off it."
plugins/lane/README.md:83-101 gives what lay.py print and lay.py write show.

decisions.what: Does O2's main path run its subagents in the foreground or in the background?
decisions.decided: In the foreground, where each start comes back once its subagent has ended. The background path, where lead is told to wait, is left off the main path.
grounds: dev/lane/trials/trying.py:84 runs Claude Code as `claude -p`, and plugins/lane/docs/flow.md:98-99 says Claude Code runs a subagent in the background by default only "in an interactive session"; how many runs of developer AIs are interactive is not known.
plugins/lane/docs/flow.md:94-96: "An Agent call of a subagent run in the foreground comes back once the subagent has ended, with the status `completed`"

decisions.decided: The developer AI asks lay.py print for the flow on step 1 of lead, writer then reviewer and back to writer while reviewer answers `more`, and sees it; once it approves, lay.py write writes the flow's sentence into step 1 and puts the check script into changelog. It asks changelog to update CHANGELOG.md for the next release. As lead starts, and as each start comes back, the check script tells lead the next move, with no stop: "changelog: The next move of the flow is move 1: start `changelog:writer`.", then move 2 for reviewer, then "changelog: reviewer answered `more`. The next move of the flow is move 1: start `changelog:writer`." while reviewer answers `more`, drawn as a loop, and "changelog: The flow is done: lane tells no more moves." once it does not. lead ends with the reviewed entries.
grounds: plugins/lane/docs/flow.md:15: "lane tells the orchestrator each move as it starts and as each start of a subagent of the flow comes back."

decisions.what: Which plugins may the document name?
decisions.decided: Lane and the example plugin changelog only; no line names Turn, Rn or another plugin of the marketplace Lane ships in.
grounds: .rn/20261013-rebuild/steering.md, T49: "lane depends on no plugin: no code, document or example of it names turn, rn or another ccpm plugin."
Lane's user is any developer AI (D1); a line naming one plugin of the marketplace would read as Lane being made for it.
